Title: no letter-case restriction.
Reverts: use GitHub's default title, Revert "original title".
Examples: [Fix] attention: Fix KV cache indexing; [Perf] [AMD] flash-attn: Optimize decode performance. -->

## Motivation
Every rank chooses its radix TreeCore on its own. The default Rust core is used only if the rank's probe passes (`_rust_fallback_reason`: platform, PyTorch, device, and `cargo --version` / `rustc -vV` with a 10 s limit); otherwise the rank falls back to the Python core. Nothing makes the ranks of one tree agree.

The probe is not reliable across ranks: `rust/rust-toolchain.toml` pins 1.92, which the current images do not ship, so the first probe installs it, and ranks that start together race on that install. In practice one rank of a worker gets the Rust core and its peers get the Python core.

The two cores are not interchangeable inside one tree. With HiCache `write_back`, `_sync_hicache_ready_counts` checks that every TP/PP rank reclaimed the same host duplicates by all-reducing a digest, and the cores fold it differently (Python: `d * 1000003 + id + 1`; Rust: `d * 1000003 + (id + 1) * 3 + component_idx`). Once the host tier fills, the first reclaim fails `write_back duplicate-reclaim victims diverged across PP/TP ranks` and the scheduler exits.
<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

## Modifications
The cache builder settles the backend for the ranks that share a prefix tree: the TP (DP-TP), attention-TP, attention-CP and PP cache groups, i.e. the groups the HiCache syncs use. Attention-DP ranks keep separate trees and are not tied together.

- `agree_tree_core_backend(params)`, called in `build_kv_cache` before the cache factory, on every rank: one MIN all-reduce of `[runtime probe ok, crc32(request), -crc32(request)]`.
  - Ranks requesting different backends fail startup.
  - If any rank's runtime probe fails, every rank uses the Python core; the result is stored in `CacheInitParams.peers_can_use_rust_tree_core`.
  - Only Rust requests probe.
- `UnifiedRadixCache` reuses that verdict: `select_tree_core_backend` then only checks the cache's own configuration (session cache, tree slots, custom components), and `create_tree_core(..., resolve=False)` skips the second rank-local probe the cache used to run.
- `check_tree_core_backend_matches(params, tree_cache)`, called right after the cache factory, on every rank: fails startup if the built backends still differ (the configuration half is decided per cache, after the factory fills the slots). Ranks whose cache has no TreeCore, such as `PureSWARadixCache` on a PP stage holding only SWA layers, take part with a neutral value.
- `_rust_fallback_reason` is split into `_rust_config_fallback_reason` and `_rust_runtime_fallback_reason`; the checks are unchanged.
- `UnifiedRadixCache.tree_core_backend` exposes the chosen backend.

Both calls run on every rank, whichever cache class it builds, so the collectives line up even when PP stages build different cache classes. Without `torch.distributed`, or with single-rank groups, nothing is communicated and behavior is unchanged. Caches built outside the builder keep the old local resolution.

Net effect: ranks that share a tree run one backend, or startup fails with a message naming the mismatch, instead of failing later during HiCache reclaim.

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->

## Accuracy Tests
No model output change: the selected backend is one of the two existing cores, and every rank of a tree now uses the same one.
<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->

## Speed Tests and Profiling
Startup only: two all-reduces of a few int64s on the CPU groups, and one fewer toolchain probe per cache.
<!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. -->

- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

+    if params.tree_core_backend is not None:

+    return envs.SGLANG_UNIFIED_RADIX_TREE_CORE_BACKEND.get()

+def _tree_peer_groups(params: CacheInitParams) -> list:
+    """The groups whose ranks share one prefix tree (those the HiCache syncs use)."""
+    dist = torch.distributed
+    if not (dist.is_available() and dist.is_initialized()):
+        return []
+    groups = []
+    for group in (
+        params.tp_cache_group,
+        params.attn_tp_cache_group,
+        params.attn_cp_cache_group,
+        params.pp_cache_group,
+    ):
+        if (
+            group is not None
+            and all(group is not seen for seen in groups)
+            and dist.get_world_size(group=group) > 1
+        ):
+            groups.append(group)
+    return groups
+
+
+def _all_reduce_min_across_tree_peers(
+    values: list[int], params: CacheInitParams
+) -> list[int]:
+    state = torch.tensor(values, dtype=torch.int64)
+    for group in _tree_peer_groups(params):
+        torch.distributed.all_reduce(
+            state, op=torch.distributed.ReduceOp.MIN, group=group
+        )
+    return state.tolist()
+
+
+# Tag of a rank whose cache has no TreeCore, e.g. PureSWARadixCache on a PP stage
+# holding only SWA layers. It is above any crc32, so in
+# check_tree_core_backend_matches such a rank takes part without winning a MIN.
+_NO_TREE_CORE_TAG = 1 << 62

+
+def agree_tree_core_backend(params: CacheInitParams) -> None:
+    """Agree the backend before the cache factory; collective on every rank.
+
+    Ranks probe the Rust toolchain on their own, and concurrent probes racing to
+    install it can fail on some ranks only. Mixed cores break the HiCache syncs
+    that assume identical trees, so one failed probe moves every rank sharing
+    the tree to Python. Ranks requesting different backends fail here.
+    """
+    requested = _requested_tree_core_backend(params)
+    reason = _rust_runtime_fallback_reason(params) if requested == "rust" else None
+    if reason is not None:
+        logger.info("Using the Python TreeCore: %s", reason)
+    tag = zlib.crc32(requested.encode())
+    runtime_ok, min_tag, neg_max_tag = _all_reduce_min_across_tree_peers(
+        [int(reason is None), tag, -tag], params
+    )
+    if min_tag != -neg_max_tag:
+        raise ValueError(
+            "Ranks sharing a prefix tree request different TreeCore backends "
+            f"(this rank: {requested!r})"
+        )
+    if requested == "rust":
+        if reason is None and not runtime_ok:
+            logger.info(
+                "Using the Python TreeCore: another rank sharing this prefix tree "
+                "cannot use the Rust TreeCore"
+            )
+        params.peers_can_use_rust_tree_core = bool(runtime_ok)
+
+
+def check_tree_core_backend_matches(params: CacheInitParams, tree_cache) -> None:

+    cache configurations could still mix cores: fail startup instead.
+    """
+    backend = getattr(tree_cache, "tree_core_backend", None)
+    tag = _NO_TREE_CORE_TAG if backend is None else zlib.crc32(backend.encode())
+    min_tag, neg_max_tag = _all_reduce_min_across_tree_peers(
+        [tag, _NO_TREE_CORE_TAG if backend is None else -tag], params
     )
-    return resolve_tree_core_backend(name, params)

+            f"(this rank: {backend!r}); make their cache configuration match or "
+            "set SGLANG_UNIFIED_RADIX_TREE_CORE_BACKEND=python"
+        )

+    reason = _rust_config_fallback_reason(params)

+        return "python"
